prompt: Some parents think it is good to give their children mobile phones while others disagree. Discuss both views and give your opinion.
essay:
Some parents believe that giving children mobile phones is beneficial, while others think that children should not have access to them. Although mobile phones can be useful for communication and education, I believe that children should only be given them at an appropriate age and with clear limits.

On the one hand, there are several advantages to giving children mobile phones. The most important benefit is that parents can easily contact their children, especially in emergencies. For example, if a child is travelling home from school alone or becomes lost, they can immediately call their parents for help. In addition, smartphones can be useful educational tools. Children can use learning applications, online dictionaries and educational videos to support their studies. Mobile phones may also help young people become familiar with technology, which is an important skill in modern society.

On the other hand, there are also significant disadvantages. Children may become addicted to their phones and spend too much time playing games, watching videos or using social media. As a result, they may spend less time studying, exercising or communicating with family members face to face. Another concern is online safety. Young children may be exposed to inappropriate content, cyberbullying or strangers on social media. Furthermore, excessive use of mobile phones, particularly before bedtime, can negatively affect children's sleeping habits and concentration.

In my opinion, completely preventing children from using mobile phones is unrealistic because technology is now an important part of everyday life. However, parents should not give smartphones to children without supervision. They should set limits on screen time, control the applications their children use and teach them how to behave safely online.

In conclusion, mobile phones can provide children with greater safety and educational opportunities, but they can also create problems such as addiction and exposure to harmful online content. Therefore, I believe children can have mobile phones as long as their parents carefully supervise their use.
